evidence.summary: On desktop a single 'Start free trial' call-to-action carries the saturated accent at the top-right of the hero.
On mobile the primary 'Start free trial' action is not above the fold; it sits behind the hamburger menu, disagreeing with the always-visible desktop placement.
Desktop top navigation order is [Product, Pricing, Docs, Sign in] left-to-right.
Mobile navigation order inside the hamburger menu is [Pricing, Product, Docs], disagreeing with the desktop order.
Bottom-anchored cookie consent banner; 'Accept all' is large and accent-colored, 'Reject all' is present but smaller and lower-contrast.
Expandable preferences panel surfaces non-essential cookie categories with several pre-ticked to 'on' by default.
Features route repeats the desktop navigation order [Product, Pricing, Docs, Sign in] and the top-right primary action.
Primary 'Start free trial' action carries the same saturated accent as on the home route.
Features hero headline is roughly 3x body scale on desktop with consistent section rhythm.
Public privacy route names the consent-management approach and corroborates the banner observed on the marketing surface.
The authenticated dashboard route was blocked and NOT inspected. No claim may rely on having observed an authenticated product screen.

limitations: The crawl was unauthenticated; the authenticated dashboard route at https://example.com/c2-saas-pilot/app/dashboard was blocked and was NOT inspected, so no claim may rely on having observed it.
Only the marketing home, features, and legal/privacy routes were inspected; the authenticated product dashboard was NOT inspected.
The observed navigation order and primary-action placement DISAGREE across desktop and mobile; the adaptation must resolve this explicitly rather than cloning either variant.
The observed consent banner pre-ticks non-essential categories and makes 'Reject all' less prominent than 'Accept all'; the adaptation must not reproduce these vendor defaults.
The snapshot is non-mutating; no cookie preference was saved and no form submission was attempted during capture.
